steps: Froze the M12 producer contract against the official JobRegistry rule that run() is the sole work-start boundary and cancel() is synchronous/idempotent but settles done only after producer cleanup.
Built a ControlledRuntime test double that records eval inputs/signals and dispose calls without starting Python.

Added RED assertions for inert spec construction, per-job AbortSignal cancellation, zero runtime.dispose() calls from job kill, and sibling job survival on one shared runtime. Production src/runtime.ts is intentionally untouched in this RED candidate.

evidence.note: Current code constructs the done Promise and calls runtime.eval during spec construction; cancel invokes runtime.dispose(), matching the reported root causes in #59/#60/#74.

limitations: Production code is intentionally not changed in this record; a successor GREEN record owns the runtime patch.

summary: GREEN candidate for #59/#60/#74: createRlmJobSpec is now inert until run(), each started Job owns one AbortController passed to runtime.eval, cancel aborts only that cell, and done settles after the existing runtime cancellation/child-cleanup barrier. No Job cancellation path calls runtime.dispose(). The real-runtime integration test now proves the shared runtime remains usable after a killed Job.

pointers: killing one job aborts only that cell
sibling job on the same runtime
M12 Issue#48/#74: a job kill settles killed and leaves the shared runtime usable

steps: Captured explicit RED on Actions before production edits.

Applied a guarded one-function patch to the large runtime file using a branch-only one-shot workflow: run() creates the AbortController and done promise; Promise.resolve().then defers runtime.eval until after synchronous hooks exist, so an immediate cancel can pre-abort without starting work.

Made cancel synchronous/idempotent by aborting only the Job controller and relying on runtime.eval's existing cancellation cleanup barrier for final settlement; removed runtime.dispose from the Job path entirely.
Updated the old M12 kill integration test so it no longer rewards whole-runtime disposal: after Job cancellation, a separate Session eval must still produce 42.
The one-shot patch workflow deleted itself in the same commit; no self-modifying workflow remains in the Candidate.

evidence.note: Intentional RED isolated the three reported lifecycle defects with no unrelated failures.
Guarded patch found the expected RED root-cause block, replaced only createRlmJobSpec plus its contradictory integration test, committed, and removed the temporary workflow.
This user-authored memory commit triggers the final Windows+Ubuntu gate inherited from merged #93.

limitations: M12 query/spawn/followup parity and Session sandbox propagation are intentionally left to #78.
One-active-RLM-Job-per-Session admission remains #86; foreground eval vs background Job coexistence policy is not changed here.
